title: Transformer downstream affordances not explored for Mamba
description: Transformer-based foundation model properties such as fine-tuning, adaptation, prompting, in-context learning, instruction tuning, RLHF, and quantization have not been explored for Mamba or selective SSMs.

verdict.reasoning: Fine-tuning/adaptation (via PEFT) is well covered by at least three papers (MambaPEFT, ProDiaL, Memba) that propose and benchmark Mamba-specific methods. Prompting/prompt-tuning is covered by MambaPEFT. In-context learning is directly tested in "Is Mamba Capable of In-Context Learning?", showing Mamba matches transformers on ICL tasks. However, three major Transformer-era affordances remain completely unaddressed: instruction tuning, RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback), and quantization (e.g., GPTQ, AWQ). These are not incremental — they are distinct paradigms with substantial literature for Transformers that have no Mamba counterpart yet. The gap has been meaningfully narrowed but not closed.

paper.title: MambaPEFT: Exploring Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mamba
paper.abstract: An ecosystem of Transformer-based models has been established by building large models with extensive data. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is a crucial technology for deploying these models to downstream tasks with minimal cost while achieving effective performance. Recently, Mamba, a State Space Model (SSM)-based model, has attracted attention as a potential alternative to Transformers. While many large-scale Mamba-based models have been proposed, efficiently adapting pre-trained Mamba-based models to downstream tasks remains unexplored. In this paper, we conduct an exploratory analysis of PEFT methods for Mamba. We investigate the effectiveness of existing PEFT methods for Transformers when applied to Mamba. We also modify these methods to better align with the Mamba architecture. Additionally, we propose new Mamba-specific PEFT methods that leverage the distinctive structure of Mamba. Our experiments indicate that PEFT performs more effectively for Mamba than Transformers. Lastly, we demonstrate how to effectively combine multiple PEFT methods and provide a framework that outperforms previous works. To ensure reproducibility, we will release the code after publication.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper provides the first comprehensive benchmarking of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for Mamba, adapting existing Transformer PEFT methods (LoRA, adapters, prompt-tuning, prefix-tuning) to the Mamba architecture and proposing new Mamba-specific methods (Affix-tuning, Additional-scan, Partial-tuning, Partial LoRA). It demonstrates that PEFT is more effective for Mamba than Transformers, and proposes a hybrid PEFT search framework. The paper covers fine-tuning, adaptation, and prompting/prompt-tuning for Mamba across both vision and language tasks.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper does not address several Transformer downstream affordances listed in the gap: (1) instruction tuning / instruction following for Mamba, (2) RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) for Mamba, (3) quantization (e.g., GPTQ, AWQ) for Mamba, and (4) in-context learning (beyond prompt-tuning, which is a different mechanism). The paper focuses exclusively on parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods and does not explore these other important Transformer-era adaptation paradigms.
evidence_snippets: In this paper, we conduct an exploratory analysis of PEFT methods for Mamba. We investigate the effectiveness of existing PEFT methods for Transformers when applied to Mamba. We also modify these methods to better align with the Mamba architecture. Additionally, we propose new Mamba-specific PEFT methods that leverage the distinctive structure of Mamba.
While many PEFT methods have been extensively studied for Transformers ... research on PEFT methods for Mamba remains limited.

To the best of our knowledge, we perform the first extensive and comprehensive benchmarking of PEFT methods for Mamba, including proposed Mamba-specific methods that are distinct from all PEFT methods for Transformers.

paper.title: Parameter Efficient Mamba Tuning via Projector-targeted Diagonal-centric Linear Transformation
paper.abstract: Despite the growing interest in Mamba architecture as a potential replacement for Transformer architecture, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches for Mamba remain largely unexplored. In our study, we introduce two key insights-driven strategies for PEFT in Mamba architecture: (1) While state-space models (SSMs) have been regarded as the cornerstone of Mamba architecture, then expected to play a primary role in transfer learning, our findings reveal that Projectors -- not SSMs -- are the predominant contributors to transfer learning. (2) Based on our observation, we propose a novel PEFT method specialized to Mamba architecture: Projector-targeted Diagonal-centric Linear Transformation (ProDiaL). ProDiaL focuses on optimizing only the pretrained Projectors for new tasks through diagonal-centric linear transformation matrices, without directly fine-tuning the Projector weights. This targeted approach allows efficient task adaptation, utilizing less than 1% of the total parameters, and exhibits strong performance across both vision and language Mamba models, highlighting its versatility and effectiveness.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper investigates parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for Mamba architectures, which directly addresses the "fine-tuning" and "adaptation" aspects of the gap. It discovers that Projectors (linear layers), not SSMs, are the dominant contributors to transfer learning in Mamba, and proposes ProDiaL, a novel PEFT method that fine-tunes Projectors via diagonal-centric linear transformations using less than 1% of total parameters. Experiments on both vision (Vim) and language (Mamba LLM) models demonstrate effectiveness across multiple downstream tasks.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper only addresses parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for Mamba. It does not explore other Transformer-compatible affordances listed in the gap: prompting, in-context learning, instruction tuning, RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback), or quantization of Mamba models. These remain entirely unexplored for Mamba/selective SSMs.
evidence_snippets: Despite the growing interest in Mamba architecture as a potential replacement for Transformer architecture, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches for Mamba remain largely unexplored.
While existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods are designed primarily for Transformer-based architectures, leaving PEFT methods tailored to Mamba largely unexplored.

In this work, we reveal that Projectors play a critical role in transfer learning within Mamba architecture. Based on our observation that fine-tuned Projectors can be approximated through a near-diagonal linear transformation, we propose ProDiaL, a novel PEFT method specifically designed for Mamba architecture.

paper.title: Is Mamba Capable of In-Context Learning?
paper.abstract: State of the art foundation models such as GPT-4 perform surprisingly well at in-context learning (ICL), a variant of meta-learning concerning the learned ability to solve tasks during a neural network forward pass, exploiting contextual information provided as input to the model. This useful ability emerges as a side product of the foundation model's massive pretraining. While transformer models are currently the state of the art in ICL, this work provides empirical evidence that Mamba, a newly proposed state space model which scales better than transformers w.r.t. the input sequence length, has similar ICL capabilities. We evaluated Mamba on tasks involving simple function approximation as well as more complex natural language processing problems. Our results demonstrate that, across both categories of tasks, Mamba closely matches the performance of transformer models for ICL. Further analysis reveals that, like transformers, Mamba appears to solve ICL problems by incrementally optimizing its internal representations. Overall, our work suggests that Mamba can be an efficient alternative to transformers for ICL tasks involving long input sequences. This is an exciting finding in meta-learning and may enable generalizations of in-context learned AutoML algorithms (like TabPFN or Optformer) to long input sequences.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper empirically evaluates Mamba's in-context learning (ICL) capabilities, comparing it to transformer models on simple function approximation tasks (linear regression, sparse linear regression, ReLU neural networks, decision trees) and more complex NLP tasks (27 tasks spanning algorithmic, knowledge, linguistic, and translation categories). It demonstrates that Mamba performs on par with transformers for ICL, and provides probing analysis suggesting Mamba solves ICL problems via incremental optimization of internal representations, similar to transformers. The paper also compares Mamba favorably against S4 and RWKV baselines.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper only addresses in-context learning, which is one of the many transformer downstream affordances listed in the gap. It does not explore: fine-tuning (e.g., full fine-tuning, LoRA, adapter-based methods), prompting techniques (e.g., chain-of-thought, few-shot prompting strategies beyond basic ICL), instruction tuning, RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback), or quantization (e.g., post-training quantization, QAT, GPTQ, AWQ). All of these remain unexplored for Mamba and selective SSMs.
evidence_snippets: Our results demonstrate that, across both categories of tasks, Mamba closely matches the performance of transformer models for ICL.

In this work, we have demonstrated that the recently proposed Mamba architecture is capable of effective in-context-learning (ICL) across tasks involving simple function approximation as well as more complex natural language processing problems.

The study's focus on simple function approximation and natural language processing (NLP) tasks raises questions about the generalizability of our findings to other domains like image or audio analysis, suggesting the need for broader research.

paper.title: Memba: Membrane-driven Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mamba
paper.abstract: State Space Models (SSMs) have emerged as powerful alternatives to attention-based Transformers, with Mamba demonstrating impressive efficiency and scalability. As these models grow increasingly larger, the need for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods becomes critical to adapt pre-trained Mamba to downstream tasks without prohibitive computational costs. However, previous approaches simply apply traditional Transformer-tailored PEFT methods without addressing the unique temporal processing dynamics of SSMs. To address this limitation, we propose Memba, a membrane-driven PEFT approach specifically designed for Mamba. Memba introduces Leaky Integrate Membrane (LIM) neurons as bio-inspired gating mechanisms that naturally accumulate membrane potentials over time, enhancing selective information retention. By strategically combining LIM neurons with Low-Rank Adaptations (LoRA) and cross-layer membrane transfer, our approach significantly improves Mamba's temporal modeling capabilities. Extensive experiments across language and vision tasks demonstrate that Memba achieves substantial improvements over existing PEFT methods. The code is available at https://github.com/Intelligent-Computing-Lab-Yale/Memba.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper proposes Memba, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) method specifically designed for Mamba models. It introduces Leaky Integrate Membrane (LIM) neurons as bio-inspired gating mechanisms combined with LoRA to adapt pre-trained Mamba to downstream tasks. The method is evaluated on language (commonsense reasoning) and vision (VTAB-1k) tasks, showing improvements over existing PEFT approaches for Mamba. This directly addresses the "fine-tuning" and "adaptation" aspects of the gap.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper only addresses parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for Mamba. It does NOT explore: (1) prompting methods (e.g., prompt tuning, prefix tuning) for Mamba, (2) in-context learning capabilities of Mamba, (3) instruction tuning of Mamba, (4) RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) applied to Mamba, (5) quantization of Mamba models, or (6) any other Transformer-compatible adaptation methods beyond LoRA-based PEFT. The gap description lists multiple Transformer downstream affordances (fine-tuning, adaptation, prompting, in-context learning, instruction tuning, RLHF, quantization), and this paper only covers one of them (fine-tuning/adaptation via PEFT).
evidence_snippets: As these models grow increasingly larger, the need for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods becomes critical to adapt pre-trained Mamba to downstream tasks without prohibitive computational costs.
While PEFT techniques have shown success in Transformer-based models~[CITE:hu2022lora] [CITE:houlsby2019parameter], their application to SSMs remains limited.
We propose \memba, a membrane-driven PEFT approach that enhances Mamba's gating mechanisms, effectively introducing temporal adaptation without modifying the core state-space components.

paper.title: MambAdapter: Lightweight Mamba-Based Adapters for Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning in Speech and Audio
paper.abstract: Fine-tuning Transformer-based foundation models has become the dominant strategy for domain adaptation in audio and speech processing. To reduce the computational and memory costs of this process, parameter-efficient transfer learning (PETL) methods have been widely explored. Meanwhile, Mamba, a recent state-space model, has emerged as a promising alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling. In this work, we present MambAdapter, a parameter-efficient transfer learning approach that integrates Mamba into low-rank bottleneck adapters. Our design combines parameter sharing across adapters with the injection of a lightweight Mamba module, enabling more effective modeling of audio features. We demonstrate that MambAdapter matches or outperforms strong PETL baselines on four audio classification tasks and five speech recognition languages, even when operating under reduced parameter budgets.

assessments.contribution_summary: The paper proposes MambAdapter, a parameter-efficient transfer learning method that inserts Mamba blocks into low-rank bottleneck adapters for fine-tuning Transformer-based audio/speech models (AST and Whisper). It shows that Mamba blocks can serve as effective components within adapters to improve adaptation performance on audio classification and speech recognition tasks. However, the paper does not explore the downstream affordances (fine-tuning, adaptation, prompting, etc.) of Mamba or selective SSM models themselves.
assessments.what_remains_open: The gap asks whether Transformer-compatible fine-tuning and adaptation methods (LoRA, adapters, prompting, in-context learning, instruction tuning, RLHF, quantization) have been explored for Mamba or selective SSM models as the backbone foundation model. This paper does not address that at all — it uses Mamba as a component within adapters attached to Transformer backbones. The core question of whether Mamba models themselves can be fine-tuned, adapted, prompted, or quantized using methods analogous to those developed for Transformers remains completely open.
evidence_snippets: We introduce MambAdapter, a highly parameter-efficient transfer learning technique that uses shared linear projections and low-rank Mamba blocks
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to incorporate Mamba as a parameter-efficient transfer learning technique into transformers.
We use MambAdapter to adapt the Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) ... and Whisper

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: All three remaining areas are well-scoped with established methodologies from the transformer literature. Instruction tuning: publicly available datasets (e.g., ShareGPT, Alpaca, Dolly) exist, and supervised fine-tuning on a pretrained Mamba model is straightforward — compute is modest (single GPU days for 7B-scale). RLHF: the standard pipeline (reward model + PPO) is architecture-agnostic; human preference datasets (Anthropic HH, HelpSteer) are available; a small team can implement it, though engineering effort is non-trivial. Quantization (GPTQ/AWQ): marginally harder because Mamba's gating and recurrent dynamics differ from attention, but weight-only quantization methods (rounding-based, calibration-data-based) can be adapted with moderate effort, and preliminary SSM quantization work already exists. All three have clear evaluation metrics (MT-Bench/IFEval for instruction tuning; harmlessness/helpfulness evals for RLHF; perplexity/task accuracy vs compression for quantization). The main barrier is that these are engineering+experimentation tasks, not requiring fundamental breakthroughs. I deduct slightly because RLHF pipelines are brittle and quantization may need architecture-specific calibration strategies, but overall these are highly tractable extensions.
